original.text: Slices are probably the most-used data structure in our codebase. You've written `append` a thousand times, and most of those times it did what you expected. document.purpose: explain when Rust code should panic and when it should return a Result

original.text: Rust gives you two ways to handle things going wrong. You can return a `Result<T, E>` and let the caller decide what to do, or you can `panic!` and stop the current thread. Newcomers often treat this as a style preference. It isn't. Each mechanism communicates something different about the failure, and choosing correctly makes your code easier to use, easier to debug, and more honest about its assumptions.
